p: Karting has become a firm favourite for birthday parties around Teesside, and it's easy to see why. It's exciting, competitive and guaranteed to get everyone talking. Whether it's a teenager's birthday, a stag do or a 40th with a twist, a little planning makes all the difference.

Start by sorting your numbers. Karting sessions are booked in slots, so confirm your headcount early and ask about party packages when you book. If your group includes a mix of experienced and nervous drivers, ask whether you can split into separate heats so everyone gets a fair race.
Give everyone a meeting time that's well ahead of your race slot. Sign-in, kit and the safety briefing all happen first, and a late arrival can hold up the whole group.
Think about food afterwards rather than before. A big meal and a fast kart aren't a great mix, and there's nothing like a post-race feast to swap stories and settle arguments over who really won.
Book ahead, as weekend slots go quickly, and check the junior rules if any youngsters are coming.

Stockton itself has a wide High Street, and the riverside along the Tees is good for a walk. Middlesbrough's town centre is just down the road too. For more railway history, Hopetown Darlington, the railway heritage attraction at North Road station, is a short drive away and tells the story of the Stockton and Darlington Railway, which opened in 1825. Its bicentenary in 2025 brought new attention to the area's proud transport heritage.
